classification.difficultyReason: Apply familiar relationships between shape and centre to the two stated distributions, recognising near equality under approximate symmetry and the upward pull of a right tail on the mean.

content.prompt: Two classes sit a test. The distribution of marks in Class A (20 students) is approximately symmetric. The distribution of marks in Class B (30 students) is positively skewed. Describe and compare how the mean and median are related in Class A and in Class B.

answer.short: In Class A, the mean and median are approximately equal. In Class B, the mean is typically greater than the median.
answer.worked: Class A has roughly balanced marks on either side of the centre, so its mean and median should be close. Class B has a tail towards higher marks. These higher marks pull the mean upwards, so the mean is typically greater than the median.
